introduction: The decline of the Indus Valley Civilization is a mysterious and debated topic in history. There was no single cause behind its decline; instead, multiple theories have been proposed. At this level, we will understand these theories in a logical and exam-oriented manner.

core_concepts.title: Aryan Invasion Theory
core_concepts.description: According to some scholars, the Aryans invaded the Indus Civilization, leading to its decline. However, this theory lacks strong archaeological evidence and is considered weak today.

core_concepts.title: Climate Change Theory
core_concepts.description: Changes in climate, such as reduced rainfall and drying up of rivers, affected agriculture and forced people to migrate gradually, leading to the decline of the civilization.

core_concepts.title: River Course Change
core_concepts.description: The drying up or shifting of the Ghaggar-Hakra (possibly Saraswati) river led to the loss of water sources, causing the collapse of urban centers.

core_concepts.title: Earthquakes and Natural Disasters
core_concepts.description: Natural disasters like earthquakes and floods may have destroyed cities, forcing inhabitants to abandon them.

core_concepts.title: Economic and Trade Decline
core_concepts.description: The decline in trade with Mesopotamia caused economic problems, weakening the civilization over time.

important_entities.name: Mortimer Wheeler
important_entities.significance: Linked skeletal remains at Harappa to invasion as a cause of decline

important_entities.name: Gordon Childe
important_entities.significance: Considered trade decline as a major cause of the civilization's fall

important_entities.name: Ghaggar-Hakra River
important_entities.significance: Its drying up is considered a major factor in the decline

important_entities.name: Mesopotamia
important_entities.significance: Breakdown of trade relations affected the economy

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume one final cause, but the decline resulted from a combination of multiple factors.
This theory is no longer widely accepted due to lack of solid evidence.
The civilization did not collapse suddenly; it declined gradually over time, which is an important exam point.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Climate, quakes, trade, Aryans all played
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps remember that multiple factors like climate change, earthquakes, trade decline, and Aryan theory contributed.
Highlights the importance of river drying or shifting in the decline.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Wheeler said invasion, Childe said trade
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Wheeler - Aryan invasion, Childe - economic decline.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks for a single most appropriate cause, prefer modern explanations like climate change.
Matching-type questions on scholars and their theories are frequently asked in exams.
